originality.rationale: Closest primary PRISM paper explicitly gives the matching degree-two residual family and empirical [3/8,29/20], while its proved sketched convergence Theorem 2 treats degree one. The new exact cubic coefficient threshold, invariant interval under arbitrary switching, and endpoint/divergence witnesses are stronger and distinct. Two contemporary general-polar acceleration methods optimize different polynomial families and do not cover this claim. Same-slot earlier claims and publicly indexed records were compared by implication; search incompleteness remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older scalar polynomial-iteration or Padé-polar result under different terminology could give the same boundary; no comprehensive literature uniqueness can be certified.
Only specific mathematical sections of original papers were materially compared; unrelated sections do not alter the explicit theorem comparison, but no claim of exhaustive inspection is made.
The new endpoint obstruction may be avoidable for a special adaptive optimizer although it is sharp for unrestricted coefficient sequences.

value.rationale: The recent original method empirically recommends a fifth-degree interval without proving its deterministic robustness. A universal pathwise guarantee independent of sketch quality plus a sharp algebraic boundary for failure is a substantive numerical stability frontier, directly controlling allowable polynomial coefficients. It is not an arbitrary finite parameter census, routine substitution, or unsupported complexity claim.
